claims.text: Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation (SCCP) can improve the strength–plasticity combination of tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
A controlled heat treatment is an effective means of inducing SCCP in tungsten-based refractory HEAs.
The starting tungsten-based refractory HEA has a single-phase or disordered matrix without pronounced nanoprecipitation.
The proposed heat-treatment protocol will promote controlled nucleation and growth of coherent nanoprecipitates throughout the alloy.
SCCP produces coherent nanoprecipitates with stepwise-controlled arrangements in the alloy matrix.
The SCCP nanoprecipitates will be uniformly dispersed throughout the matrix.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces relieve stress concentrations that could otherwise cause premature crack initiation.
The nanoprecipitates increase alloy strength through precipitation hardening.
Relieving stress concentrations delays crack initiation and thereby improves tensile ductility.
At ambient temperature, an SCCP tungsten refractory HEA can achieve tensile strength above 2 GPa while retaining approximately 15% tensile ductility.
The specified tensile-strength and ductility targets should also hold at around 800 °C.
An SCCP tungsten refractory HEA can retain a yield strength of about 1.05 GPa at 800 °C.
The SCCP-treated alloy will outperform an as-cast or otherwise non-SCCP single-phase tungsten refractory HEA in both strength and ductility.
The strength–plasticity improvement requires precipitates to remain coherent and within an optimal size and volume-fraction range.
Overgrown or incoherent precipitates may prevent improvement of the strength–plasticity combination.
The required heat-treatment time and temperature profile and the scalability of the approach across refractory HEA compositions are uncertain.
Comparison of SCCP-treated and untreated samples by TEM, XRD, and room- and high-temperature tensile testing can test the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement in both tensile strength and ductility relative to the untreated control would falsify the predicted performance improvement.
Failure to form the intended coherent nanoprecipitates would by itself falsify the hypothesis.
